title: “DBT Tribal Portal and Tribal Scholarship Disbursement”
body_text:
Union Minister for Tribal Affairs Shri Durgadas Uikey informed Rajya Sabha that currently, the Ministry is already leveraging the benefit of DBT Tribal Portal by accessing the data of beneficiaries submitted by the respective State/UT for monitoring and generating MIS reports for the implementation of pre-matric and post-matric scholarship schemes. The States/UTs have also been given facilities to upload queries, documents, utilization certificates, statement of expenditure etc. which has reduced processing time and reduced grievances. The details of the number of beneficiaries reported by the States/UTs on the DBT Tribal Portal for the pre-matric and post-matric scholarship schemes during the last three financial years are given at Annexure-I.
The Pre-Matric and Post-Matric Scholarship Schemes are the Centrally Sponsored Schemes and implemented through respective States/UTs. The disbursement of scholarships is carried out by the concerned State/UT through their own portal or NSP portal. The progress made through the Portal are given as under: -
End-to-End Digitization: Transition from paper-based processing to scheme-specific digital portals. Common Data Standard: Implementation of standard data format for seamless web-service API based data sharing between States/UT portals/ National Scholarship Portal (NSP) and the DBT Tribal Portal of the Ministry Faster Communication and Online Processing: Online upload of Utilization Certificates (UCs), Statements of Expenditure (SoE), and queries by States, significantly reducing processing time and administrative delays. Public Transparency & Outcome Dashboards: Integration of beneficiary and transaction data with the Performance Dashboard of the Ministry, DBT Mission, Prayas Dashboard, and NITI Aayog for outcome tracking.
The data of beneficiaries reported by the State/UTs in the DBT Tribal Portal have been useful for monitoring and generating MIS reports. Integration of National Scholarship Portal with States/UTs scholarship portal enables data validation and automated deduplication checks across schemes and databases.
Under Pre-Matric and Post-Matric Scholarship Schemes for ST students, to eliminate parking of funds at State level, minimize delays in release of scholarship, and ensure transparency of fund flow, the Ministry has adopted the SNA SPARSH Model for release of central share under Pre-Matric and Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme. This serves as a Just-in-Time Disbursement Framework under which the Central Share funds are release in "Just-in-time" as and when the bills are raised by respective State Govt for payment of scholarship. Once the bills for scholarship payment is approved, both Central Share as well as State Share fund is directly transferred from RBI account to Student beneficiary account on through DBT. This eliminates the parking of central share funds at state level and minimize delay in disbursement of scholarship.
Under Central Sector Schemes of Scholarship implemented directly by the Ministry, a robust digital mechanism is established through the National Scholarship Portal (NSP), Ministry’s Scholarship Portal and the Public Financial Management System (PFMS) to facilitate Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT).
Removal of physical application process and manual verification by Institute/District/State authorities has streamlined approval workflows and reduced the overall application processing time. Transfer of Scholarship amount through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) into the beneficiary student bank accounts ensures that financial benefit reaches targeted ST students in time and without involvement of intermediaries.

enrichment.summary: In a Rajya Sabha reply, Union Minister for Tribal Affairs Durgadas Uikey detailed how the Ministry uses the DBT Tribal Portal to monitor and generate MIS reports for Pre-Matric and Post-Matric Scholarship Schemes for ST students, implemented as Centrally Sponsored Schemes through States/UTs. He highlighted digitization measures including the SNA SPARSH 'Just-in-Time' disbursement model that transfers central and state scholarship shares directly to student accounts to eliminate fund parking and delays, alongside integration with NSP, PFMS, and various dashboards. Annexure data showed beneficiary numbers fluctuating across states from FY2023-24 to 2025-26, with Pre-Matric totals of ~6.36 lakh, ~9.52 lakh, and ~7.40 lakh, and Post-Matric totals declining from ~17.84 lakh to ~15.91 lakh.
enrichment.context: The Pre-Matric and Post-Matric Scholarship Schemes for Scheduled Tribe students are key welfare instruments under the Ministry of Tribal Affairs aimed at reducing dropout rates and promoting access to education among tribal youth, who face historically lower literacy and enrollment rates. The DBT (Direct Benefit Transfer) architecture, including the National Scholarship Portal (NSP) and Public Financial Management System (PFMS), was developed to plug leakages, remove intermediaries, and ensure timely fund transfer—addressing long-standing complaints of delayed disbursement that often caused students to drop out mid-session. The SNA SPARSH (Single Nodal Agency - Sparsh) model is part of a broader Finance Ministry-driven reform for Centrally Sponsored Schemes, ensuring central funds are not idly parked in state treasuries but released only when actually needed, improving cash management and accountability across schemes beyond just tribal welfare (it is also applied in other CSS domains like education and health). This reform aligns with the government's broader push for cooperative fiscal federalism combined with technology-enabled governance (e-governance), and ties into the Digital India and Direct Benefit Transfer Mission's larger goals of transparency and reduced corruption in welfare delivery. The fluctuating and sometimes declining beneficiary numbers, along with gaps in reporting by some states, point to persistent challenges in last-mile scheme implementation despite improved digital infrastructure.

prelims_questions.question: The 'SNA SPARSH' model, mentioned in the context of scholarship disbursement for Scheduled Tribe students, primarily aims to:
options: Provide interest-free loans to tribal students for higher education
Ensure Just-in-Time release of central funds directly to beneficiaries, avoiding parking of funds at the state level
Establish tribal residential schools under the Eklavya Model Schools scheme
Recruit teachers for tribal welfare hostels
prelims_questions.explanation: As per the release, SNA SPARSH is a Just-in-Time Disbursement Framework where central and state scholarship funds are transferred directly from the RBI account to the student's bank account via DBT, eliminating fund parking at the state level.

prelims_questions.explanation: The release specifically mentions NSP, PFMS, and the DBT Tribal Portal as part of the digital DBT mechanism for scholarship disbursement; Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission is unrelated to this scheme.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the significance of Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) mechanisms in improving the delivery of welfare schemes for Scheduled Tribes in India. Examine the role of the SNA SPARSH model in addressing the problem of fund parking and delayed disbursement in Centrally Sponsored Schemes.

Despite technological upgrades such as the DBT Tribal Portal and National Scholarship Portal, beneficiary data for tribal scholarship schemes show significant year-on-year fluctuations across states. Analyze the structural and administrative challenges that persist in the last-mile delivery of welfare benefits to Scheduled Tribe students.
